sources.title: Attention Is All You Need
sources.notes: Foundational Transformer paper; predates current chat post-training, long-context, and serving practice and is not product-behavior evidence.

sources.title: SentencePiece: A simple and language independent subword tokenizer and detokenizer for Neural Text Processing
sources.notes: One tokenizer family; consequences depend on the model's actual training tokenizer and template.

sources.title: Neural Machine Translation of Rare Words with Subword Units
sources.notes: Early machine-translation BPE study; not a universal tokenizer prescription or product-quality result.

sources.title: Model optimization
sources.notes: Provider-specific living guidance used for its evaluate-improve loop, not API permanence or universal process authority.

sources.title: Holistic Evaluation of Language Models
sources.notes: Broad benchmark framework whose scenarios and models age; task-specific product release evidence remains necessary.

sources.title: Working with evals
sources.notes: Provider-specific evaluation implementation; datasets and regression loops are expressed provider-neutrally in this book.

sources.title: Define success criteria and build evaluations
sources.notes: Provider guidance; criteria and evaluation methods need consequence-specific validation and cannot prove complete coverage.

sources.title: Writing a chat template
sources.notes: Implementation guide; the correct template is model-specific and must match training format.

sources.title: Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts
sources.notes: Position findings vary by task and model; current candidates require fresh testing and the paper is not a universal ordering rule.

sources.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
sources.notes: Original RAG formulation and benchmark setup; reported results do not transfer automatically to current stacks or Mosaic Desk.

sources.title: RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation
sources.notes: Automated RAG metrics and evaluator models require calibration; metric labels do not prove ground truth or authority.

sources.title: Aya Model: An Instruction Finetuned Open-Access Multilingual Language Model
sources.notes: Reported multilingual coverage and results do not establish equal capability across languages or transfer to Mosaic Desk.

sources.title: Tülu 3: Pushing Frontiers in Open Language Model Post-Training
sources.notes: One open-model recipe and evaluation suite; methods and results require reproduction for a target base model and task.

sources.title: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models
sources.notes: One adaptation method; reported efficiency and quality are model and task dependent and do not select a Mosaic method.

sources.title: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning methods
sources.notes: Implementation catalog; not all methods support all models, layers, quantization, or hotswap paths.

sources.title: QLoRA: Efficient Finetuning of Quantized LLMs
sources.notes: Hardware, model, optimizer, and evaluation assumptions bound the reported efficiency and quality.

sources.title: Direct Preference Optimization: Your Language Model is Secretly a Reward Model
sources.notes: Method assumptions and comparisons are task and model dependent; preference data encode values and biases.

sources.title: Distilling the Knowledge in a Neural Network
sources.notes: Foundational general method; modern generative distillation has additional data, decoding, and evaluation concerns.

sources.title: Don't Stop Pretraining: Adapt Language Models to Domains and Tasks
sources.notes: Pre-generative encoder-oriented experiments; useful for the decision, not a promise of modern LLM gains.

sources.title: Automatic Mixed Precision
sources.notes: Operator and hardware support and numerical behavior vary; behavior evaluation remains required.

sources.title: FlashAttention: Fast and Memory-Efficient Exact Attention with IO-Awareness
sources.notes: Kernel and hardware implementation concerns are adjacent depth; reported speedups depend on workload and platform.
